sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A large evergreen conifer native to the mountains from northern Türkiye to the western Caucasus. In cultivation it is commonly listed at about 12–18 m tall; exceptional native trees exceed 60 m. Its flat, dark-green needles have pale stomatal bands underneath. A reliable crown width for wild trees was not located.

sections.title: Uses and related firs
sections.text: It is widely grown as an ornamental and Christmas tree. Like Abies alba, it has upright cones that disintegrate on the tree; A. alba is native to Europe, while this species is native farther east, from Türkiye to the western Caucasus. The sources consulted do not establish food use or toxicity of its parts.
